//: EXAMPLE: a customer index of STRUCTURED RECORDS whose field names we do not know in advance.
Every field name below (record_id, record_type, display_name, payload_json, ...) is a
PLACEHOLDER. Replace each one with the real column name in the customer index; the `mapping`
block is what tells this capability which physical field plays which logical role, so nothing
in the code has to know the customer's naming.
Load it as part of a registry, alongside the RAG index declaration:
ENGAGEMENTS_INDEX_SCHEMAS=C:\path\to\index-config-dir
RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=search
or as a comma/semicolon separated list of explicit files:
ENGAGEMENTS_INDEX_SCHEMAS=C:\cfg\rag-index.json,C:\cfg\records-index.json
ONE INDEX FOR EVERYTHING vs ONE INDEX PER KIND - both work:
- one index for all record kinds: keep every kind in `mapping.entityType` below, in ONE file.
- one index per kind: copy this file per index, set a distinct `id` and `indexName`, and set
the kinds that index does NOT hold to null. A record kind may be claimed by at most one
declaration; claiming it twice is a hard error naming both files. So a contacts index sets
"contact": "<value>", "event": null and an events index does the reverse.
`contact` and `event` must always be PRESENT (possibly null) so the split is deliberate; the
reference kinds may simply be omitted.
NOTE files named *.example.json are SKIPPED when a directory is expanded, so copy this file to
a new name (e.g. records-index.json) before dropping it into a config directory.
Check it before running anything against Azure - `validate` is offline and prints every
declaration in the registry:
npm run provision:search -w @greenhouse-resume-builder/cap-engagements-mcp-engagements -- validate
NEVER run `provision:search ensure|sync|reindex` against a customer index - `ensure` would try
to reshape it and `sync` would push demo seed records into it.
//fields: Describes the index EXACTLY as it exists in Azure. `filterable`/`searchable` are checked here
BEFORE an OData $filter is emitted, so a mismatch fails with a readable message instead of an
opaque HTTP 400. Declare a field only if the real index has it.
type: Edm.String | Edm.Int32 | Edm.Int64 | Edm.Double | Edm.Boolean |
//mapping: Every value here must name a field declared in `fields` above.
key       REQUIRED. The index key field. Must be the one field with "key": true.
entityType  The discriminator that separates record kinds inside one index.
.field    REQUIRED (when entityType is present), must be `filterable` - the column holding
the kind, e.g. record_type.
.contact  REQUIRED key - the VALUE stored in that column for contact rows, or null when this
index holds no contacts (another declaration must then claim them).
.event    REQUIRED key - the VALUE stored for event rows, or null as above.
.leader / .topic / .message / .region
OPTIONAL - the VALUE for each reference kind. Omit one (or set it null) and that
record set reads back EMPTY; it is NEVER substituted from the demo seed.
Omit the whole entityType block for a document/chunk RAG index (see the grounding example).
topicIds  OPTIONAL, must be `filterable` and a Collection(Edm.String) - the tags used to narrow
recall to a subject area. Omitted => topic narrowing is skipped, not faked.
status    OPTIONAL, must be `filterable` - the relationship state (active / prospect).
Omitted => the status filter is skipped.
payload   OPTIONAL but needed by the planner - a field holding the FULL record as a JSON
string. Reads reconstruct domain objects from it. When it is absent, read queries
fail with a clear message rather than returning half-populated records.
grounding OPTIONAL and NOT set here - this declaration is structured records only. Put the
grounding block on the RAG index declaration; at most one declaration may carry it.
Free-text search targets every field declared `searchable` in THIS declaration, so add the
customer's name/org/expertise/location columns above to make them reachable by query text.
